title: Final fast.2 native timing and accuracy evidence with Kaiser series

units.cpu_s: process CPU seconds summed over threads

notes: All 17 final-native benchmark reports, all 33 unprofiled API repetitions, both additional profiles, and both final 19-case audits are retained. No spectra or input sample arrays are included.

Final stage is identified by native SHA256 b0ab2e54; c41db40c is the previous first fast.2 integration recorded in results_fast2.json. These labels are library fingerprints, not Git commit abbreviations.

Raw-source identifiers and hashes allow comparison with the untracked source files. Relative ../lpsd_kaiser_experiments identifiers refer to the adjacent experiment directory. The curated measurements remain usable without those raw files.

Audit code and fast/original source hashes were verified against the stated source commit during curation. The measurement reports do not record a Git commit; source equality, not assumed chronology, establishes this source anchor.
File mtimes are filesystem metadata, not an independent measurement-clock record. Exact audit timestamps are copied from their reports.

API timers exclude imports, input generation, warm-up, fingerprints, and file output. Setup and warm-up times are retained. Audit calls are numerical checks, not controlled wall-time benchmarks, and their reports do not provide per-case execution times.
CPU times are process CPU summed over threads. RSS is a process-lifetime high-water mark; it is not per-call allocation. The concurrency working budget is not a hard process-RSS cap.

W8 phase sums overlap in time and must not be read as wall time. C preparation/segments subdivide C kernel time; window generation/sums subdivide window_and_sums. Never add parent and child phase totals. Length bands are derived from raw frequency rows.

W8 automatic-budget profile records its actual budget and peak reservation. W1/W2/W4 and paired W8 runs use an explicit 4096 MiB budget; the scaling comparison therefore changes budget as well as worker count.
All main timings use Linux x86_64, GCC 13.3.0 and the recorded native build flags. They do not establish ARM, Apple, portable-wheel, or other-machine speedups.
Environment installed-distribution metadata can name fast.1 while the loaded module is fast.2; loaded-module metadata and binary/source fingerprints identify the measured implementation.

Baseline fast.1 has no measurement-time build sidecar. Its post-measurement binary fingerprint, ELF compiler identity, pinned source hashes, and reconstructed flags are copied from the first dataset and the binary fingerprint was rechecked at final curation. This is weaker provenance than the final sidecars.

The paired PSD Kaiser results support a modest additional API improvement; standalone generator speedups and window-phase speedups are not whole-API speedups. PSD-only did not consistently outperform all outputs.

The final 1M series median is worse than the earlier c41 median. Boxcar10M improves versus fast.1, while the earlier Boxcar1M regression remains visible in results_fast2.json. No universal size/window claim follows.

Accuracy reference uses the unchanged scalar path and a separate original-C anchor. Frequencies match exactly. Raw relative maxima, counts at or above 1%, absolute-only acceptance counts, nonfinite and changed-zero counts remain visible.

Combined acceptance is abs(candidate-reference) < 0.01*abs(reference) OR abs(candidate-reference) <= explicit absolute allowance. Identical zeros pass; nonfinite pairs fail. Exactly 1% relative error alone fails.

PSD absolute allowance 1e-24 and NSD allowance 1e-12 apply only to the fixed synthetic signal amplitudes and output units in these audits. They are not general defaults, signal-peak-scaled floors, or a universal 1% guarantee.
No runtime accuracy retry or scalar fallback was used. Metadata kaiser_method=series_with_fallback means formula fallback for unsupported Kaiser parameters, not an accuracy-triggered DFT rerun.

Accuracy case parameters inherit n/sample_rate/n_frequencies/n_averages from the audit configuration; one frequency hash represents the exactly matching candidate/reference grids. All audited density arrays are float32.

Diagnostic points deduplicate extrema, ranked relative points and exceptional points by frequency index using roles. Arbitrary zero-error locations are omitted; every numerical summary, count, status and output fingerprint remains retained.

baseline_fast1_native.limitation: Baseline reports contain no build sidecar or at-measurement binary hash. The current baseline binary was fingerprinted after measurement; compiler identity comes from its ELF comment. Flags are reconstructed from the pinned builder and the coordinator-reported native build mode, not recovered from a compiler-command log.

paired_kaiser_10m_w8.conclusion: Series PSD beat previous PSD in all three pairs, but PSD-only did not beat all outputs consistently. Three pairs do not establish a confidence interval or a universal speedup.

worker_scaling_10m.conclusion: Eight workers gave the lowest median for this 10M workload; process CPU time and RSS increased. W8 used the automatic memory budget, while W1/W2/W4 used 4096 MiB; this is not an isolated worker-count experiment.

dataset_sizes.conclusion: These cross-stage series were not paired. The final 1M median regressed versus c41; 30M improved modestly with overlapping ranges. Neither supports a universal Kaiser-series API gain.

boxcar_10m.conclusion: The final fast/PSD 10M case improved versus fast.1 auto/all. Version, kernel and outputs change together. The earlier Boxcar 1M regression remains in results_fast2.json.

w1_profile_comparison.conclusion: Faster window generation is a phase result, not the whole-API speedup. C segments remain dominant; the single final profiled call took more segment time than the previous profile. Profile totals are separate calls, not the unprofiled medians.

accuracy.conclusion: All 38 cases pass the explicit combined policy; 35 pass the strict relative-only policy. HFT248D spectral nulls retain large relative differences accepted solely through the fixed absolute allowances.
